rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a Ni coating on W surfaces before consolidation, while the paper uses liquid-metal dealloying of a WTaVTi alloy in molten Cu to create a composite. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions (coating vs. dealloying).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis mentions heating cycles up to 700°C and irradiation, while the paper uses 1200°C liquid-metal dealloying, thermal conductivity up to 800°C, and 25 keV He+ irradiation. The broad regime of high-temperature processing and irradiation testing is shared, but the specific conditions (temperature, atmosphere, irradiation type) differ substantially.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes a Ni interlayer improving bonding and reducing void formation, whereas the paper's mechanism involves selective Ti dissolution, W-rich interlayer formation, and aligned Cu channels. These are different general classes of mechanism (coating-based interfacial bonding vs. dealloying-driven phase separation and passivation).
rationale.outcome_agreement: Both predict improved thermal conductivity relative to an untreated baseline, but the hypothesis predicts improvement for a W–Cu composite with Ni coating, while the paper predicts improvement for a dealloyed RHEA–Cu composite surpassing pure W at high temperature. The property and direction are the same, but the specific comparison and magnitude differ.
